newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurostocks end with big losses after Wall St.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurostocks end with big losses after Wall St.

text.p: European stocks ended trade with hefty losses on Tuesday, disheartened by a big drop on Wall Street where American investors cashed in profits after last week's record-breaking run.
On the foreign exchanges, the dollar, still buoyed by expectations over a soft single European currency, gained on the mark in late European deals but drifted lower against the yen.

European bourses, trading in the red for most of the day, were dragged down further by Wall Street's negative performance. London and Paris plunged by nearly 1.5 percent at one stage and Frankfurt's IBIS index of electronic trade was down one percent.

New York's losses came despite a batch of U.S. economic figures which showed subdued inflationary pressures. Investors took the opportunity to pocket some of the gains from last week's big advance which set six closing records.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down about 0.5 percent within minutes of the U.S. data showing that consumer inflation and housing starts for May came in lower than expected.

"I think it is basically selling on the news," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co in New York. "There is nothing to suggest it's inflationary and it's not a cause for concern."

London, which itself set a cracking pace last week with three closing records, suffered the most from Wall Street. The market already had enough worries about possible bad news in the British budget next month.

The FTSE 100 index of leading shares finished down 62.9 points at 4,682.2, its biggest one-day loss since April 1, and the market was expected to remain in a selling mood after reports that the government could cut tax breaks for pension funds in the July 2 budget.

"We're only three weeks away from the budget now and I think the market will continue to be nervous," said one trader. "We still look vulnerable to more profit-taking because there's a lot of profits to be taken."
Paris also had a rough day. The blue-chip CAC-40 index, which touched a trading record in volatile trade on Monday, ended 33.27 points down at 2,762.27 after strong advances last week.
"We're seeing profit-taking on recent gains as the market waits for the new government's policy address" on Thursday, a broker said.
Frankfurt floor trade, which ended before Wall Street opened, finished down 0.63 percent.
But after-hours trading on the IBIS index fell further after New York's drop and an outbreak of jitters about the effectiveness of the single currency stability pact agreed at the Amsterdam summit.
"There is a lot of nervousness around and a lot of it is related to the negotiations at the Amsterdam summit," said one trader.
In currencies, the dollar shrugged off the U.S. data which kept prospects of higher interest rates at bay and held gains of half a pfennig against the mark.
The German currency remains under pressure and the dollar is benefiting from its safe haven reputation as the stability pact improved prospects for a weak single currency.

"There was nothing too impressive in the CPI data, it really just confirms the U.S. is still in a low-inflation scenario, putting the argument for a U.S. rate hike any time soon on to the backburner," said a dealer.

The U.S. currency was weakened a little against the yen with traders focusing on this week's Japanese May trade data, expected to show a growing surplus, and U.S. April figures, where a worsening deficit, is expected.

Anticipation of the data has made for speculation that sparks will fly when leaders of the Group of Seven industrial nations meet in Denver on June 20-22. The market fears that the expanding trade gap will spark a row between the United States and Japan as the stronger dollar puts Japanese exports at an advantage.
Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered, said the United States was concerned about trade but not to the point that it was willing to engage heavily in exchange rate rhetoric.
"The issue is to try to get Japan to boost demand and how they do that, rather than by trying to engineer a manipulation of exchange rates," said Fox.
CURRENCIES AT EUROPEAN CLOSE
The dollar was at 1.7340 marks and 113.23 yen, compared with 1.7291 and 113.39 in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was finished down 62.9 points at 4,682.2.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was closed down 33.27 points at 2,762.60.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended down 23.63 points at 3,741.48.
PRECIOUS METALS AT EUROPEAN CLOSE
Gold closed at $342.35 an ounce, compared with Monday's close of $341.75. Silver was at $4.80, up eight cents.
